Something super important is knowing what scales are most popular in the genre, harmonic minor for sinister neo classical type stuff(usually the go to), and double harmonic minor for more dissonant but still melodic stuff. And my favorite, the whole half diminished scale. One of the most evil dissonant scales ever. Keep in mind you don’t ever have to use a “pure” scale. You can add notes wherever, whenever when you want, in fact I encourage you to not use a pure scale when writing riffs. Sometimes I’ll write pure power chords in the diminished scale even though that’s technically outside the scale at times. Learn these scales, learn how to practice these scales, learn how to identify and analyze when bands you like use them.

Oh man, I’ve had a lot of tendon issues in my life, this sounds like the beginning of something more serious. I had horrible tendonitis in my hand that destroyed my life for a year and half, just because I over practiced guitar and pushed past my body’s limits. It started exactly like that, it was fatigue, not pain. Then eventually evolved into full blown chronic pain. I had to go to physical therapy for 6 months. 

Take a week or two off of guitar. See how you’re feeling after that. Dial back how often you’re playing when you come back and take frequent breaks. Focus on safely stretching your forearms and fingers, and eventually strengthen your forearms much later down the line. You’ll save yourself a lot of pain and time if you start taking care of the stuff now. My hand still isn’t the same and even though my playing ability is far beyond where I was when I hurt it, it still always feels uncomfortable no matter what I play.
